What is a point of contact?

seeds.ex: Contact, interaction, and channel. Help pages use contact for the person and interaction for the full conversation on a channel. Digital is a specific family of channels, not a synonym for every non-voice contact. On the digital routing page, a contact is the person interacting with an agent, IVR, or bot. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: On the digital routing page, a contact is the person interacting with an agent, IVR, or bot.

seeds.ex: Tenant, business unit, and campaign. A tenant is the high-level grouping for support, billing, and global settings. Skills are created inside a campaign. API calls then discover which area that tenant lives in. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The Admin welcome page describes a tenant as the high-level organizational grouping used to manage technical support, billing, and global settings for your NiCE CXone sys

seeds.ex: Browser, WebRTC, and allowlists. Integrated Softphone is the NiCE application. WebRTC is the Chrome technology it uses. Those names are not interchangeable, and Integrated Softphone has an IP allowlist. If the agent leg is VoIP, NiCE CXone offers two softphone options. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: If the agent leg is VoIP, NiCE CXone offers two softphone options. Integrated Softphone is built into the platform, so there is nothing to install on the agent computer.

seeds.ti: SIP, in the language CXone and the RFC share
seeds.ex: SIP, in the language CXone and the RFC share. RFC 3261 is the SIP specification. NiCE's connectivity page uses SIP trunk as a virtual PBX-to-carrier connection. The lab does not invent CXone SIP headers that the help page does not list. SIP is specified in RFC 3261. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: SIP is specified in RFC 3261. That document is the place to learn INVITE, responses, and dialogs. NiCE's connectivity page does not reprint the RFC.

seeds.ex: The Admin application. Admin is where employees, roles, login authenticators, and access keys are managed. The app selector is how you get there. The users and security page says the Admin application manages general components of the system. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The users and security page says the Admin application manages general components of the system.

seeds.ex: Roles and least privilege. Permissions live on roles. An API user gets a unique role with only the permissions the integration uses. An access key inherits that power. Security settings that control what users can see and do are roles and permissions. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: Security settings that control what users can see and do are roles and permissions.

seeds.ex: External identity providers. Users can authenticate with an external IdP. Applications authenticate with access keys. The help page lists the OIDC endpoints you copy from the IdP, including end-session for single logout. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: If you do not have a discovery document, the external IdP page tells you to enter Issuer, JsonWebKeySet, Authorization, Token, UserInfo, Revocation, and End Session endpo

seeds.ex: Public Preview, formerly Controlled Release. Starting with the 26.3 release, the Controlled Release program is named Public Preview. Features on a release page may still require that program or a license. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The 26.3 release notes say that starting with that release, the NiCE CXone Controlled Release program is known as Public Preview.

seeds.ti: Employee attributes that turn features on
seeds.ex: Employee attributes that turn features on. A role is not the only switch. Digital agents need the Digital Engagement attribute. Salesforce screen-pop needs Agent Integrations and Customer Card. Those attributes can also be how you are billed. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: Digital Channels says agents need a supported agent application, permissions for each channel, the Digital Engagement attribute on the employee profile, and assignment to

seeds.ex: The inbound voice order. Set Up Inbound Voice builds a phone skill, a phone script, and a point of contact, in that order. The DNIS already has to exist. Set Up Inbound Voice says to create an inbound phone ACD skill with Media Type Phone Call and direction Inbound, pick a campaign, and name the skill. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: Set Up Inbound Voice says to create an inbound phone ACD skill with Media Type Phone Call and direction Inbound, pick a campaign, and name the skill.

seeds.ex: Skill name, campaign, and direction. A skill has a media type, a direction, a name, and a campaign. Priority fields, including acceleration, live on the skill and are not the same thing as proficiency. Create New > Single Skill. Media Type Phone Call. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: Create New > Single Skill. Media Type Phone Call. Inbound/Outbound set to Inbound. Enter a skill name. Select the campaign.

seeds.ex: Permissions along the setup path. The inbound page names skill and POC permissions, and script create permission. A person who can build a script may still be unable to attach it. Skill work: ACD > Skills Create, Edit. Script work, on the setup page: ACD > Contact Settings > Scripts Create. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: Skill work: ACD > Skills Create, Edit. Script work, on the setup page: ACD > Contact Settings > Scripts Create.

seeds.ex: Employee profiles. An employee has a first name, last name, an email-shaped username, and a primary role. Special characters the getting-started page lists are rejected in names. Admin, Employees, Create Employee. First and last name are required. Middle name is optional. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: Admin, Employees, Create Employee. First and last name are required. Middle name is optional.

seeds.ex: MAX and Agent Workspace. Current help still names MAX and a family of Agent Workspace applications. Digital support is not identical across them. AutoSummary lists the ones it works with. Agents use MAX or the Agent Workspace suite. The page says MAX supports all available digital channels. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: Agents use MAX or the Agent Workspace suite. The page says MAX supports all available digital channels.

seeds.ex: Make one agent digitally ready. Four checks: supported app, channel permission, Digital Engagement, and the digital skill. Missing any one of them looks like a routing bug. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: Digital Channels lists the agent requirements together: a supported application, permissions for each channel, the Digital Engagement attribute, and assignment to the rou

seeds.ex: ScreenAgent beside the voice recording. ScreenAgent records the screen. From version 2.1.40 it can mask the screen when voice is masked, so a paused voice recording does not leave the sensitive screen in the file. Recording Management supports audio and screen for quality and compliance. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: Recording Management supports audio and screen for quality and compliance. ScreenAgent records and monitors screen activity.

seeds.ex: Personal Connection acceleration is zero. Personal Connection skills set acceleration to 0 because there is no queue of contacts. Initial priority still matters for blending. Dialing by proficiency is a separate pair of checkboxes. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The static delivery page says: for Personal Connection skills, set acceleration to 0 because there is no queue of contacts.

seeds.ti: Script types and the POC contract
seeds.ex: Script types and the POC contract. You create a script for a media type. Phone scripts serve phone POCs. One digital script type serves digital channels. The POC selects exactly one. A script is created for a media type. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: A script is created for a media type. The POC is assigned one script, and that script must define the flow from the start of the interaction.

seeds.ex: BEGIN, MENU, REQAGENT, MUSIC, WAIT. The basic tutorial is a menu, a skill request per branch, and music until answer. The Classics bullseye insert is Music for 90 seconds and then UpdateContact. Menu plays a prompt, prerecorded, TTS, or both, and stores the contact's entry in the variable you name. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: Menu plays a prompt, prerecorded, TTS, or both, and stores the contact's entry in the variable you name. The sample is sales, support, and billing.

seeds.ex: Promote without surprising production. Production is the script name on the POC. A lab export from Contact Path is not a Studio import. Say both things in the change ticket. The builder exports labSchema cxone-lab.studio/1 and a flag that it is not an official Studio export. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The builder exports labSchema cxone-lab.studio/1 and a flag that it is not an official Studio export. NiCE's cited pages do not document this file as an import.

seeds.ti: Virtual hold, as the product page states it
seeds.ex: Virtual hold, as the product page states it. The Studio integration page says virtual hold can disconnect the caller and create a callback when an agent is free, so the caller does not wait on the line. It does not list the action's properties there. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: NiCE CXone Studio, on the integrations page, says advanced actions include Estimated Wait Time and Virtual Hold.

seeds.ex: The official basic script. The tutorial checks that an agent can help, plays a menu, requests an agent, and plays music until answer. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: Develop a Basic Script says the script verifies at least one agent can handle the call, presents a menu, requests an agent after the selection, and plays hold music until

seeds.ex: ASR, named and not over-specified. Studio Fundamentals defines ASR as automatic speech recognition that lets contacts respond by speaking, pressing keys, or both. This lesson does not invent a speech-tuning guide. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: Studio Fundamentals says ASR allows contacts to respond to prompts by speaking, pressing phone keys, or both.

seeds.ti: Music, virtual hold, and estimated wait
seeds.ex: Music, virtual hold, and estimated wait. Three different waits: music until answer, a 90-second bullseye beat, and virtual hold as a callback. Estimated wait is named, not specified. The tutorial plays music until an agent answers. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The tutorial plays music until an agent answers. The Classics example uses a 90-second Music action as the beat before UpdateContact, not as the whole wait.

seeds.ex: Digital Experience versus legacy channels. Digital is the Digital Experience family. Legacy phone, email, and chat keep their own script types. Do not mix the POC forms. Digital means any channel, contact, or skill associated with Digital Experience. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: Digital means any channel, contact, or skill associated with Digital Experience. The digital channels page contrasts digital skills with all non-digital ACD skills, and d

seeds.ex: Workflow automation beside Studio. WFA rules run independent of Studio and can assign skills. Studio remains the recommended way to manage the contact. Use both on purpose. Digital Routing says WFA rules run independent of Studio scripts. You can use both to customize handling. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: Digital Routing says WFA rules run independent of Studio scripts. You can use both to customize handling.

seeds.ex: Outbound digital still uses queues. Do not delete every queue. Outbound digital routing still uses them. WFA assigns the skill used when the contact replies. Digital Routing says the system still uses routing queues to route outbound interactions. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: Digital Routing says the system still uses routing queues to route outbound interactions.

seeds.ex: Stereo is the default. Recording Management supports stereo by default and mono as well. Stereo records participants separately so analytics and one-sided playback are possible. This lesson does not invent codecs. Recording Management supports both stereo, by default, and mono recording. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: Recording Management supports both stereo, by default, and mono recording. The page says stereo lets you use analytic solutions, record participants separately, and play

seeds.ti: Hold is a gap, not a failure
seeds.ex: Hold is a gap, not a failure. Calls on hold are not recorded, including hold music. Recording resumes when the agent returns. A consultation during that hold is recorded. When an agent puts a caller on hold, the recording stops. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: When an agent puts a caller on hold, the recording stops. No audio from the hold period is captured, including hold music or anything the caller hears.

seeds.ti: Engagement Hub feeds QM from other systems
seeds.ex: Engagement Hub feeds QM from other systems. Engagement Hub brings PABX, ACD, CRM, digital, and dialer data into CXone so Supervisor, Copilot for Supervisors, QM, and WFM can use it. Engagement Hub connects third-party systems such as PABXs, ACDs, CRMs, digital channels, and dialers to CXone. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: Engagement Hub connects third-party systems such as PABXs, ACDs, CRMs, digital channels, and dialers to CXone.

seeds.ex: Playback rules you can defend. A hold gap, a mask blank, and a third-party path are three different playback stories. Cloud storage is named. Retention numbers from other pages are not borrowed. Silence during hold is expected. A blank screen during a mask is expected from ScreenAgent 2.1.40. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: Silence during hold is expected. A blank screen during a mask is expected from ScreenAgent 2.1.40.

seeds.ti: TTS voices and a knowledge base
seeds.ex: TTS voices and a knowledge base. Standard TTS voices are in the subscription. Premium voices are bring-your-own. A knowledge base needs Knowledge Hub. This lesson does not invent prices. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: Standard voices for Autopilot (Omilia) on the page include Omilia native, Google Standard, WaveNet, and Neural2, Microsoft Neural, and AWS Standard and Neural.

seeds.ex: What setup actually requires. An account representative enables AutoSummary and Agent Assist Hub. You then need a profile, Studio, skills with disposition, and a transcription profile. MAX also needs a Copilot for Agents license. You work with the account representative for the initial enablement. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: You work with the account representative for the initial enablement. Agent Assist Hub must be enabled.

seeds.ex: Getting Started is a sequence. The developer Getting Started path is plan, register, a test user, authentication, discovery, and best practices. Registration is typically a few business days. This lesson does not invent a portal SLA. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: Getting Started walks you through planning the integration, registering the application, creating a test user, choosing authentication, discovering your tenant's endpoint

seeds.ti: Discover the issuer, then the tenant
seeds.ex: Discover the issuer, then the tenant. Start at the global issuer or the FedRAMP issuer, append OpenID configuration, and read token_endpoint. The tenant id from the ID token selects the CXone configuration. Do not hard-code na1. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The global issuer on the authentication page is https://cxone.niceincontact.com. Append /.well-known/openid-configuration.

seeds.ti: Refresh early and pin the key id
seeds.ex: Refresh early and pin the key id. Plan to renew before 5 minutes of access-token expiry. expires_in of 3600 is a sample. Verify JWTs with JWKS, cache keys 15 to 30 days, and reject an unknown kid. The token response includes expires_in. A sample on the page is 3600 seconds. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The token response includes expires_in. A sample on the page is 3600 seconds. The page also says each exchange can return a different lifetime, so you read the value you

seeds.ti: Studio API actions are not the whole catalog
seeds.ex: Studio API actions are not the whole catalog. Some APIs have Studio actions. Verb colors are documented. If no action exists, the traditional path is Snippet or a REST call. GET NEXT EVENT is for agent-application events. Not every API has an action. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The API actions page colors verbs: POST green, PUT orange, GET blue, DEL red, PATCH aqua. A purple shield marks security.

seeds.ti: Salesforce wants Lightning and the console
seeds.ex: Salesforce wants Lightning and the console. Agent Workspace for Salesforce is Lightning only. Console navigation keeps records on one screen. Standard navigation opens a new browser tab per interaction. The Salesforce Agent Workspace page says the integration is only available in Salesforce Lightning. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The Salesforce Agent Workspace page says the integration is only available in Salesforce Lightning. The org should use console navigation, not standard navigation.

seeds.ti: Einstein is a virtual agent, not the CRM screen
seeds.ex: Einstein is a virtual agent, not the CRM screen. Salesforce Einstein connects through Virtual Agent Hub and TextBot Exchange for digital chat. It is not the same project as Agent Workspace inside Lightning. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The Einstein page connects Salesforce Einstein as a virtual agent through Virtual Agent Hub and TextBot Exchange. The channel is digital chat.

seeds.ti: Ticketing currently names Salesforce and Zendesk
seeds.ex: Ticketing currently names Salesforce and Zendesk. CRM Ticketing needs a license and Ticket Search permission. The FAQ says Salesforce and Zendesk are the supported CRMs. Users and name changes belong in the CRM. Tickets import when solved, and 90 days is the retention. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: You need a CRM Ticketing license and the Search & Playback > Search > Ticket Search permission. Tickets are searched in the Interactions application.

seeds.ti: Salesforce Voice 26.3 needs one IndexedDB delete
seeds.ex: Salesforce Voice 26.3 needs one IndexedDB delete. Upgrading the Salesforce Voice package from 26.2.8 or earlier to 26.3 requires deleting the IndexedDB database nice-cxone-ccf once. Package dates are not the whole platform's dates. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The IndexedDB page says that upgrading the Salesforce Voice package from 26.2.8 or earlier to 26.3 requires deleting the IndexedDB database named nice-cxone-ccf once.

seeds.ti: Numbers, RespOrg, and the voice PoP
seeds.ex: Numbers, RespOrg, and the voice PoP. The preferred toll-free path is to make CXone the RespOrg. Local numbers can be ported. Other arrivals are remote call forwarding, an independent carrier, or your PBX. A voice PoP is the carrier's PSTN gateway. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The preferred option is to authorize CXone as the Responsible Organization for the toll-free numbers you want to use. Local numbers can be ported if you want that.

seeds.ti: The carrier, the PoP, and CXone are three owners
seeds.ex: The carrier, the PoP, and CXone are three owners. The carrier brings the internet and the voice PoP. CXone starts when the number, email, or chat is a point of contact. SIP header recipes and OPTIONS timers are not in the connectivity page. The carrier is the company that provides the internet connection. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The carrier is the company that provides the internet connection. The voice PoP is that carrier's PSTN gateway. A SIP trunk connects your PBX to the carrier.

seeds.ti: Two migrations get confused on purpose
seeds.ex: Two migrations get confused on purpose. A WFM connector copies agent state and history. Multi-ACD records a phone system you keep. Migrated Calls uploads old recordings. None of those pages is a full ACD cutover cookbook. The Cisco UCCE connector and the Avaya CMS pages feed Workforce Management. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The Cisco UCCE connector and the Avaya CMS pages feed Workforce Management. Engagement Hub and the Multi-ACD table record or process a third-party phone system.

seeds.ti: The UCCE connector is on premises and speaks SQL
seeds.ex: The UCCE connector is on premises and speaks SQL. The connector page supports Cisco Unified CCE 11.6. Real-time adherence uses the Cisco connector. Historical skills use SQL every 15 minutes. Intraday is not supported. Outbound dialer, fax, SMS, and web are no. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The connector is on-premise software. It receives agent state from the Cisco ACD and relays it for real-time adherence.

seeds.ti: Avaya CMS and Avaya CMS Legacy are different connectors
seeds.ex: Avaya CMS and Avaya CMS Legacy are different connectors. The current Avaya CMS page is an SDK over REST, inbound voice only, with intraday. The legacy ASC is version 19, on premises, SQL on Informix, and intraday is not supported. The Avaya CMS page connects through the SDK. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The Avaya CMS page connects through the SDK. Real-time and historical methods are REST APIs, at 15 minutes. Intraday is used in Intraday Manager.

seeds.ti: The supervisor badge comes through Club One
seeds.ex: The supervisor badge comes through Club One. CXone Supervisor Certification is free and foundational. Its scope names WFM, QM, Dashboard, Coaching, and Gamification. Club One is the supervisor community that hosts it, not a catalog of every technical exam. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The Credly badge for CXone Supervisor Certification describes a free foundational certification reached through Club One.

seeds.ti: 26.3 and 26.4 disagree if you force one calendar
seeds.ex: 26.3 and 26.4 disagree if you force one calendar. 26.3 moved to 2 September 2026 through 5 November 2026. Coming Soon for 26.4 begins 26 October 2026 and targets 4 February 2027. Those windows overlap. Controlled Release becomes Public Preview in 26.3. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The 26.3 notes say the cycle was originally 3 August 2026 to 25 October 2026 and, after a moratorium, 2 September 2026 to 5 November 2026. Features can change.

seeds.ti: Turn dynamic delivery on, and do not casually turn it off
seeds.ex: Turn dynamic delivery on, and do not casually turn it off. The business unit's Contact Handling Method becomes Dynamic Delivery (Recommended). After that, NiCE recommends asking the account representative before you go back to static delivery. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The enable page's required permission is ACD > ACD Configuration > Business Unit Time Zones.

seeds.ti: Channel lock, elevation, and integrated matching
seeds.ex: Channel lock, elevation, and integrated matching. Channel lock turns AND into OR. Elevation has a table. Integrated matching compares voice, work items, and digital by priority, and it is on by default for new systems. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: With channel lock off, an agent whose Total Contact Count is 3 can have one voice interaction and two chats at the same time.

seeds.ti: The live table is only the current state
seeds.ex: The live table is only the current state. RTA shows the current scheduled activity beside the current actual activity. A break that already ended is not on that table. Schedule edits show up almost immediately. The Real Time Adherence page requires WFM > General Permissions > Real Time Adherence set to ON. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The Real Time Adherence page requires WFM > General Permissions > Real Time Adherence set to ON. The table is a side-by-side of scheduled and actual activities.

seeds.ex: Activity adherence or category adherence. A tenant uses one approach. If the category columns are on the table, adherence compares categories. Otherwise it compares activities. The page prints both examples. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The Real Time Adherence page says adherence is either activity-based or category-based, and only one is active.

seeds.ti: Fix the live row from Schedule Manager
seeds.ex: Fix the live row from Schedule Manager. If the agent should be on break, change the activity in Schedule Manager and publish. RTA updates almost immediately. The CSV export covers up to 30 days and leaves unmapped activities uncalculated. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The Real Time Adherence page says you can put the agent back in adherence by editing the current activity in Schedule Manager and publishing.

seeds.ti: Forms, plans, and no retention rule
seeds.ex: Forms, plans, and no retention rule. Quality Management builds forms and plans, then can lead to coaching. The welcome page says there is no defined rule for how long evaluations must be kept. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The Quality Management welcome page says you build evaluation forms and plans, distribute interactions for evaluation, and may then design coaching.

seeds.ex: 70 percent is not 73.3333. The welcome page walks Sanity QA through both formulas. Averaging the percentages gives 70. Averaging the points gives 73.3333. The page's Vijay figures do not match each other. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The welcome page's percentage table gives Sanity QA 3 ÷ 5 × 100 = 60% and 8 ÷ 10 × 100 = 80%.

seeds.ti: A form is questions, then an activation
seeds.ex: A form is questions, then an activation. Forms can be standard, self-assessments, or collaborative. A draft cannot be used. A critical answer can fail the whole evaluation. The supervisor review window on the form settings is 30 days. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: Form Manager says a form is a collection of questions used to evaluate interactions.

seeds.ti: Beginning, end, and three seconds of silence
seeds.ex: Beginning, end, and three seconds of silence. Overall sentiment is the whole interaction. Beginning sentiment is the first 400 words or the first 30 percent, whichever comes first. End sentiment is the last 30 percent. Mixed is not available on the beginning or the end. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The Improve Sentiment page says you can filter a workspace by Positive, Negative, Neutral, or Mixed sentiment, and by when it occurred. Overall is the whole interaction.

seeds.ex: The Salesforce CTI adapter URL. Agent Workspace for Salesforce is Lightning only. The install creates two call centers. The non-FedRAMP CTI adapter URL and the FedRAMP URL are different hosts. Anything under 365 pixels wide is not supported. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The install page says Agent Workspace for Salesforce runs in Salesforce Lightning and is compatible with Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, and Marketing Cloud.

seeds.ex: Trusted URLs and Click2Jack. Salesforce must trust cxagent.nicecxone.com and api.incontact.com. Click2Jack wants your own Lightning and My Domain hosts. It can block non-agent users who still carry NiCE components. The install page says to add cxagent.nicecxone.com and api.incontact.com as trusted URLs. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The install page says to add cxagent.nicecxone.com and api.incontact.com as trusted URLs.

seeds.ex: CPaaS stays confirm. No NiCE help page opened for this chapter uses CPaaS as a product name. The Agentic Engagement Plane is a real, different page. Five9 and Webex Contact Center stay confirm. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: A search for a CXone CPaaS page returned the connectivity page, the UCaaS (1CX) page, and the Agentic Engagement Plane.

seeds.ti: Glossary words from the connectivity page
seeds.ex: Glossary words from the connectivity page. On an inbound call the A leg is the contact side and the B leg is the agent side. A transfer adds a second B leg. Cluster examples on the page are C14, E39, and M33. The connectivity page says the A leg is the portion between the contact and NiCE CXone. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: The connectivity page says the A leg is the portion between the contact and NiCE CXone. On an inbound call that leg is ingress.

seeds.ex: Sister technologies this chapter opened. The sisters in this chapter are the products whose pages were opened for it: WFM, QM, Interaction Analytics, Integration Hub, UCaaS, Salesforce CTI, and the Agentic Engagement Plane. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
seeds.eg: CXone WFM, on the pages this chapter uses, forecasts and schedules, then compares the schedule with ACD events. Quality Management builds forms and plans.

docs.eg: Contacts, points of contact, skills, scripts, and the network facts you need before you touch Admin.
