docs.ti: AHT, service level, and the numbers routing serves
docs.ex: AHT, service level, and the numbers routing serves. WFM forecasts volume and average handle time, then you choose a speed-of-answer target. A tighter target needs more agents. Routing features such as bullseye change who is eligible, which can change the forecast. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: General Forecast says you review historical data, and forecasting predicts volume and average handle time.

docs.ti: How to read a help page and a release note
docs.ex: How to read a help page and a release note. Major releases happen four times a year. Dates on the 26.3 and 26.4 pages do not line up cleanly. This lab marks that clash instead of smoothing it over. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The release process page says a cycle runs from the Coming Soon notes until the release reaches the last customer cluster.

docs.ex: Platform, licensing, and releases. Tenants, roles, access keys, and how to read a release note without sanding off the dates. These are themed worlds inside Contact Path.
docs.eg: Tenants, roles, access keys, and how to read a release note without sanding off the dates.

docs.ex: The Admin application. Admin is where employees, roles, login authenticators, and access keys are managed. The app selector is how you get there. The users and security page says the Admin application manages general components of the system. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The users and security page says the Admin application manages general components of the system.

docs.ti: Licenses the help pages actually name
docs.ex: Licenses the help pages actually name. Some features say they need a license. This lab lists only licenses a cited page names, and it does not invent SKUs or prices. CRM Ticketing says the feature is available if you have a CRM Ticketing license. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: CRM Ticketing says the feature is available if you have a CRM Ticketing license. Migrated Calls refers to an Interactions Upload license and to Admin > Recording > Upload

docs.ex: Roles and least privilege. Permissions live on roles. An API user gets a unique role with only the permissions the integration uses. An access key inherits that power. Security settings that control what users can see and do are roles and permissions. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Security settings that control what users can see and do are roles and permissions.

docs.ex: External identity providers. Users can authenticate with an external IdP. Applications authenticate with access keys. The help page lists the OIDC endpoints you copy from the IdP, including end-session for single logout. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: If you do not have a discovery document, the external IdP page tells you to enter Issuer, JsonWebKeySet, Authorization, Token, UserInfo, Revocation, and End Session endpo

docs.ex: Public Preview, formerly Controlled Release. Starting with the 26.3 release, the Controlled Release program is named Public Preview. Features on a release page may still require that program or a license. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The 26.3 release notes say that starting with that release, the NiCE CXone Controlled Release program is known as Public Preview.

docs.ex: Access keys are not passwords. A person logs in with a password or an IdP. A back-end app sends an access key id and secret to the token endpoint. The global token URL comes from OpenID discovery, not from a guess. Getting Started says a back-end app provides an access key id and secret. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Getting Started says a back-end app provides an access key id and secret. For client_secret_basic, you send a basic authorization header with the application's client id

docs.ti: Employee attributes that turn features on
docs.ex: Employee attributes that turn features on. A role is not the only switch. Digital agents need the Digital Engagement attribute. Salesforce screen-pop needs Agent Integrations and Customer Card. Those attributes can also be how you are billed. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Digital Channels says agents need a supported agent application, permissions for each channel, the Digital Engagement attribute on the employee profile, and assignment to

docs.ex: ACD setup. The inbound voice path: skill, script, DNIS, and the point of contact that binds them. These are themed worlds inside Contact Path.
docs.eg: The inbound voice path: skill, script, DNIS, and the point of contact that binds them.

docs.ex: The inbound voice order. Set Up Inbound Voice builds a phone skill, a phone script, and a point of contact, in that order. The DNIS already has to exist. Set Up Inbound Voice says to create an inbound phone ACD skill with Media Type Phone Call and direction Inbound, pick a campaign, and name the skill. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Set Up Inbound Voice says to create an inbound phone ACD skill with Media Type Phone Call and direction Inbound, pick a campaign, and name the skill.

docs.ex: Skill name, campaign, and direction. A skill has a media type, a direction, a name, and a campaign. Priority fields, including acceleration, live on the skill and are not the same thing as proficiency. Create New > Single Skill. Media Type Phone Call. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Create New > Single Skill. Media Type Phone Call. Inbound/Outbound set to Inbound. Enter a skill name. Select the campaign.

docs.ex: Bind the point of contact. The point of contact is the only object that joins a specific number to one skill and one script. Reporting for IVR presses is a flag on that object. App selector, ACD, Contact Settings, Points of Contact, Create New, Single Point of Contact. Media type Phone Call. Name it. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: App selector, ACD, Contact Settings, Points of Contact, Create New, Single Point of Contact. Media type Phone Call. Name it. Pick the DNIS. Pick the skill you created.

docs.ti: Hours, closed paths, and what this lab will not invent
docs.ex: Hours, closed paths, and what this lab will not invent. The inbound page says you may add an IVR in the script and that you may need an account representative. It does not, in the passage used here, document an hours action field by field. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The basic script tutorial builds a menu, requests an agent, and plays hold music until the agent answers.

docs.ti: The script the POC actually runs
docs.ex: The script the POC actually runs. A beautiful script that is not selected on the point of contact does not run. The POC holds exactly one script name. The inbound setup's last move is selecting the script on the point of contact. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The inbound setup's last move is selecting the script on the point of contact. Studio Fundamentals says scripts assigned to POCs must define the flow from the start of th

docs.ex: Campaigns hold skills. The skill form requires a campaign. Reporting and later staffing talk about skills. The campaign is the folder you chose at create time. Set Up Inbound Voice tells you to select the campaign the skill should be part of. It does not, in that procedure, ask you to create the campaign. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Set Up Inbound Voice tells you to select the campaign the skill should be part of. It does not, in that procedure, ask you to create the campaign.

docs.ex: Permissions along the setup path. The inbound page names skill and POC permissions, and script create permission. A person who can build a script may still be unable to attach it. Skill work: ACD > Skills Create, Edit. Script work, on the setup page: ACD > Contact Settings > Scripts Create. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Skill work: ACD > Skills Create, Edit. Script work, on the setup page: ACD > Contact Settings > Scripts Create.

docs.ex: People, teams, and agent apps. Employees, proficiency, digital attributes, and the agent applications the help pages still name. These are themed worlds inside Contact Path.
docs.eg: Employees, proficiency, digital attributes, and the agent applications the help pages still name.

docs.ex: Employee profiles. An employee has a first name, last name, an email-shaped username, and a primary role. Special characters the getting-started page lists are rejected in names. Admin, Employees, Create Employee. First and last name are required. Middle name is optional. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Admin, Employees, Create Employee. First and last name are required. Middle name is optional.

docs.ti: Assign a skill and a proficiency
docs.ex: Assign a skill and a proficiency. Assignment is not complete at the skill name. Bullseye needs a proficiency from 1 to 20, and 1 is best. The Classics example starts at 1–5 and widens to 1–8. On the bullseye page, Marguerite sets the fiction skill's REQAGENT to HighProficiency 1 and LowProficiency 5. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: On the bullseye page, Marguerite sets the fiction skill's REQAGENT to HighProficiency 1 and LowProficiency 5. Music plays for 90 seconds.

docs.ex: MAX and Agent Workspace. Current help still names MAX and a family of Agent Workspace applications. Digital support is not identical across them. AutoSummary lists the ones it works with. Agents use MAX or the Agent Workspace suite. The page says MAX supports all available digital channels. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Agents use MAX or the Agent Workspace suite. The page says MAX supports all available digital channels.

docs.ex: Who can see a recording. Seeing a recording is a permission question. The Admin page says agents may see only their own interactions while supervisors see more. Recording Management is a separate product surface. The Admin page says access to recordings and interactions is typically permission-based. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The Admin page says access to recordings and interactions is typically permission-based. Agents may view only their own.

docs.ti: Teams, views, and what we will not invent
docs.ex: Teams, views, and what we will not invent. Supervisors are described as having broader visibility. The Admin page also names views as a security tool. This lesson does not invent a team-hierarchy feature the page does not describe. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The Admin page lists views next to roles, login authenticators, and access keys as the way you manage security and data access.

docs.ex: Make one agent digitally ready. Four checks: supported app, channel permission, Digital Engagement, and the digital skill. Missing any one of them looks like a routing bug. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Digital Channels lists the agent requirements together: a supported application, permissions for each channel, the Digital Engagement attribute, and assignment to the rou

docs.ex: ScreenAgent beside the voice recording. ScreenAgent records the screen. From version 2.1.40 it can mask the screen when voice is masked, so a paused voice recording does not leave the sensitive screen in the file. Recording Management supports audio and screen for quality and compliance. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Recording Management supports audio and screen for quality and compliance. ScreenAgent records and monitors screen activity.

docs.ex: Skills and routing. Priority math, bullseye, routing attributes, and the Personal Connection exception. These are themed worlds inside Contact Path.
docs.eg: Priority math, bullseye, routing attributes, and the Personal Connection exception.

docs.ex: Priority and acceleration. Overall priority is (Time × Acceleration) + Initial Priority, capped by Maximum Priority. The published three-minute example lands on 7. The static delivery page says acceleration is how fast priority rises. The default is 1. The minimum is 0. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The static delivery page says acceleration is how fast priority rises. The default is 1. The minimum is 0. Maximum priority caps the result.

docs.ex: Bullseye with proficiency. Bullseye adds and removes agents by proficiency, routing attributes, or both. COUNTAGENTS, GETQUEUE, REQAGENT, and UpdateContact can carry it. Bullseye can use skill proficiency, routing attributes, or both. Proficiency is assigned with the skill. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Bullseye can use skill proficiency, routing attributes, or both. Proficiency is assigned with the skill.

docs.ex: Personal Connection acceleration is zero. Personal Connection skills set acceleration to 0 because there is no queue of contacts. Initial priority still matters for blending. Dialing by proficiency is a separate pair of checkboxes. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The static delivery page says: for Personal Connection skills, set acceleration to 0 because there is no queue of contacts.

docs.ex: Routing attributes. Attributes are custom traits on agents. The bullseye page uses language as the example beside proficiency. They are not skills, and they are not OAuth scopes. Marguerite uses proficiency for fiction-book knowledge and routing attributes for language. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Marguerite uses proficiency for fiction-book knowledge and routing attributes for language.

docs.ex: Static delivery priorities. The priority page is filed under static delivery. Inbound and digital skills can use the three settings. Personal Connection with priority blending uses a different trio of priority fields. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The static delivery page says an inbound or digital skill can use the three settings.

docs.ex: Blending, bullseye, and the forecast. Initial priority ranks work when you blend. Bullseye changes who can take it. The forecast assumed a pool. Change one and you owe the WFM team a look. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: General Forecast lets you build alternative forecasts with What-If, using the same parameters and history while you change forecast data. You can compare staffing plans.

docs.ti: What this lab will not claim about delivery
docs.ex: What this lab will not claim about delivery. The simulator breaks ties by longest idle. Personal Connection documents wait time, simultaneous calls, and optional proficiency. A universal inbound tie-break is not stated on the pages cited here. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The proactive voice page says PC distributes calls using the agent's wait time, current simultaneous calls, and optionally proficiency.

docs.ex: Studio scripting. Actions, branches, API actions, and a lab canvas that does not pretend to be an import file. These are themed worlds inside Contact Path.
docs.eg: Actions, branches, API actions, and a lab canvas that does not pretend to be an import file.

docs.ti: Script types and the POC contract
docs.ex: Script types and the POC contract. You create a script for a media type. Phone scripts serve phone POCs. One digital script type serves digital channels. The POC selects exactly one. A script is created for a media type. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: A script is created for a media type. The POC is assigned one script, and that script must define the flow from the start of the interaction.

docs.ex: BEGIN, MENU, REQAGENT, MUSIC, WAIT. The basic tutorial is a menu, a skill request per branch, and music until answer. The Classics bullseye insert is Music for 90 seconds and then UpdateContact. Menu plays a prompt, prerecorded, TTS, or both, and stores the contact's entry in the variable you name. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Menu plays a prompt, prerecorded, TTS, or both, and stores the contact's entry in the variable you name. The sample is sales, support, and billing.

docs.ti: API actions are not help pages
docs.ex: API actions are not help pages. API actions call CXone REST APIs from Studio. They are not documented as action help. Use the developer portal. Not every API has an action. API actions sit on the API Actions palette. POST is green, PUT orange, GET blue, DEL red, PATCH aqua. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: API actions sit on the API Actions palette. POST is green, PUT orange, GET blue, DEL red, PATCH aqua. Security-related actions show a purple shield.

docs.ti: Trace the contact, not the picture
docs.ex: Trace the contact, not the picture. A script picture can be wrong in three cited ways: the POC points elsewhere, Reqagent skill is blank, or the proficiency window excludes the idle agents. Trace those before you trace packets. First confirm the point of contact names this script. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: First confirm the point of contact names this script. Second confirm each Reqagent names the skill you think, because blank means the POC skill.

docs.ex: Digital scripts. Digital scripts plus digital skills are the preferred inbound method. Workflow automation can run beside them. Update Contact Digital does not accelerate priority. Digital Routing says Studio and workflow automation work together. WFA rules run independent of scripts. You can use both. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Digital Routing says Studio and workflow automation work together. WFA rules run independent of scripts. You can use both.

docs.ex: Promote without surprising production. Production is the script name on the POC. A lab export from Contact Path is not a Studio import. Say both things in the change ticket. The builder exports labSchema cxone-lab.studio/1 and a flag that it is not an official Studio export. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The builder exports labSchema cxone-lab.studio/1 and a flag that it is not an official Studio export. NiCE's cited pages do not document this file as an import.

docs.ti: Virtual hold, as the product page states it
docs.ex: Virtual hold, as the product page states it. The Studio integration page says virtual hold can disconnect the caller and create a callback when an agent is free, so the caller does not wait on the line. It does not list the action's properties there. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: NiCE CXone Studio, on the integrations page, says advanced actions include Estimated Wait Time and Virtual Hold.

docs.ex: IVR. Menus, prompts, reporting, and the wait treatments the pages actually describe. These are themed worlds inside Contact Path.
docs.eg: Menus, prompts, reporting, and the wait treatments the pages actually describe.

docs.ex: What Menu stores. Menu plays a prompt and writes the contact's choice into a variable you name. Branches use that value. The Menu page says the value entered is stored in a variable created by the action. You name it in the Variable property. The script then takes the branch for that value. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The Menu page says the value entered is stored in a variable created by the action. You name it in the Variable property. The script then takes the branch for that value.

docs.ex: IVR reporting on the POC. IVR Reporting Enabled on the phone point of contact tracks press paths for that number. It is not a Studio action. Set Up Inbound Voice says to select IVR Reporting Enabled if calls to this number should track IVR press paths. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Set Up Inbound Voice says to select IVR Reporting Enabled if calls to this number should track IVR press paths.

docs.ex: The official basic script. The tutorial checks that an agent can help, plays a menu, requests an agent, and plays music until answer. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Develop a Basic Script says the script verifies at least one agent can handle the call, presents a menu, requests an agent after the selection, and plays hold music until

docs.ex: ASR, named and not over-specified. Studio Fundamentals defines ASR as automatic speech recognition that lets contacts respond by speaking, pressing keys, or both. This lesson does not invent a speech-tuning guide. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Studio Fundamentals says ASR allows contacts to respond to prompts by speaking, pressing phone keys, or both.

docs.ti: Music, virtual hold, and estimated wait
docs.ex: Music, virtual hold, and estimated wait. Three different waits: music until answer, a 90-second bullseye beat, and virtual hold as a callback. Estimated wait is named, not specified. The tutorial plays music until an agent answers. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The tutorial plays music until an agent answers. The Classics example uses a 90-second Music action as the beat before UpdateContact, not as the whole wait.

docs.ex: Closed paths stay honest. You can specify a closed experience. You cannot invent the hours action. The account representative is the page's offer of help for IVR beyond the basic script. A closed path should say whether the caller hears a message, leaves a message, or is offered a callback. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: A closed path should say whether the caller hears a message, leaves a message, or is offered a callback.

docs.ex: Press-path lab. Combine the menu, the POC flag, and one test call per branch. Reporting without the flag, or a flag without distinct skills, wastes the test. Write the digit, the variable value, the skill, and the agents who have that skill. The tutorial's rule is that the skill matches the destination. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Write the digit, the variable value, the skill, and the agents who have that skill. The tutorial's rule is that the skill matches the destination.

docs.ex: Digital channels. Skills replaced new inbound queues. One script type. Agents need four things. These are themed worlds inside Contact Path.
docs.eg: Skills replaced new inbound queues. One script type. Agents need four things.

docs.ex: Digital Experience versus legacy channels. Digital is the Digital Experience family. Legacy phone, email, and chat keep their own script types. Do not mix the POC forms. Digital means any channel, contact, or skill associated with Digital Experience. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Digital means any channel, contact, or skill associated with Digital Experience. The digital channels page contrasts digital skills with all non-digital ACD skills, and d

docs.ex: The Summer 2023 routing change. Before Summer 2023, digital inbound work used routing queues. New inbound configuration uses skills and scripts. Queues remain for outbound, and old inbound queues still sync. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Digital Routing says that prior to the Summer 2023 release, digital contacts were primarily routed with routing queues.

docs.ex: Workflow automation beside Studio. WFA rules run independent of Studio and can assign skills. Studio remains the recommended way to manage the contact. Use both on purpose. Digital Routing says WFA rules run independent of Studio scripts. You can use both to customize handling. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Digital Routing says WFA rules run independent of Studio scripts. You can use both to customize handling.

docs.ti: Skill, script, and the digital POC
docs.ex: Skill, script, and the digital POC. A new digital channel needs a digital skill and a digital script as defaults. The script may change the skill later. Digital Channels says that to set up a new POC you need a digital ACD skill and a Studio script as the default. They are only the starting point. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Digital Channels says that to set up a new POC you need a digital ACD skill and a Studio script as the default. They are only the starting point.

docs.ex: Outbound digital still uses queues. Do not delete every queue. Outbound digital routing still uses them. WFA assigns the skill used when the contact replies. Digital Routing says the system still uses routing queues to route outbound interactions. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Digital Routing says the system still uses routing queues to route outbound interactions.

docs.ex: The agent's four digital checks. Supported app, channel permission, Digital Engagement, and the skill. MAX is the app the page says supports all available digital channels. Digital Channels lists the application, the permissions, the attribute, and the queues or skills. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Digital Channels lists the application, the permissions, the attribute, and the queues or skills.

docs.ti: Widen a digital pool without acceleration
docs.ex: Widen a digital pool without acceleration. Update Contact Digital widens proficiency from 1 to 20, 1 best, and its priority does not accelerate. Use WFA if digital priority must move. Update Contact Digital updates priority and proficiency ranges to broaden the pool. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Update Contact Digital updates priority and proficiency ranges to broaden the pool. Priority is entered from 0 to 1000 and does not have acceleration.

docs.ex: Workforce management. Forecast volume and AHT, staff to a target, and keep IEX as a different product. These are themed worlds inside Contact Path.
docs.eg: Forecast volume and AHT, staff to a target, and keep IEX as a different product.

docs.ex: What CXone WFM is for. CXone WFM forecasts, schedules, and checks adherence. The welcome page lists the modules and a 10,000-agent scale. IEX is a different application. The welcome page says CXone WFM manages and forecasts agent schedules. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The welcome page says CXone WFM manages and forecasts agent schedules. After agents and groups are set up you forecast, edit, and generate a schedule.

docs.ex: Forecast volume and AHT. History becomes a volume and AHT forecast. You need at least three months, and the page also recommends at least 13 weeks. Then you generate staffing. Accurate results need at least three months of historical data. When you define the period, the page recommends at least 13 weeks. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Accurate results need at least three months of historical data. When you define the period, the page recommends at least 13 weeks.

docs.ti: The service target is a staffing choice
docs.ex: The service target is a staffing choice. The page's example is answering in under 10 seconds instead of 30. The tighter target needs more people. Bullseye can change who those people are. Lowering average speed of answer needs more agents. So does raising dials. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Lowering average speed of answer needs more agents. So does raising dials. The staffing plan is the last step of that story.

docs.ex: Schedules, bids, and time off. After the forecast you edit and generate the schedule. Agents can bid on shifts. Time off is requested and reviewed. The welcome page names those jobs without this lesson inventing the screens. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The welcome page says you forecast, edit, and generate a schedule, create bids agents can bid on, review time-off requests, and check adherence.

docs.ex: Real-time adherence. RTA compares agent state to the schedule. The UCCE and Avaya connectors exist so a non-CXone ACD can feed that picture. Historical adherence is a separate pull. Real-Time Adherence is one of the modules certified at the 10,000-agent scale. It is not the forecast and not the script. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Real-Time Adherence is one of the modules certified at the 10,000-agent scale. It is not the forecast and not the script.

docs.ti: IEX is not a skin on CXone WFM
docs.ex: IEX is not a skin on CXone WFM. The welcome page sends IEX users to help inside IEX. Bullseye sends them to the Distribution Rules Guide. Do not screenshot one product to train the other. Workforce Management (IEX Integrated) has its own help, inside the application. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Workforce Management (IEX Integrated) has its own help, inside the application. The CXone WFM welcome page says so in the first lines.

docs.ti: Hand a routing change to WFM
docs.ex: Hand a routing change to WFM. A one-page note is enough: priorities, windows, PC at acceleration 0, and which product. What-If is optional. Silence is how the Monday schedule goes wrong. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Include initial priorities, the formula you used, PC acceleration 0 if outbound is blended, and the proficiency window before and after the wait.

docs.ex: Quality and recording. Stereo and mono, the hold gap, ScreenAgent masks, and what QM is allowed to claim. These are themed worlds inside Contact Path.
docs.eg: Stereo and mono, the hold gap, ScreenAgent masks, and what QM is allowed to claim.

docs.ex: Stereo is the default. Recording Management supports stereo by default and mono as well. Stereo records participants separately so analytics and one-sided playback are possible. This lesson does not invent codecs. Recording Management supports both stereo, by default, and mono recording. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Recording Management supports both stereo, by default, and mono recording. The page says stereo lets you use analytic solutions, record participants separately, and play

docs.ti: Hold is a gap, not a failure
docs.ex: Hold is a gap, not a failure. Calls on hold are not recorded, including hold music. Recording resumes when the agent returns. A consultation during that hold is recorded. When an agent puts a caller on hold, the recording stops. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: When an agent puts a caller on hold, the recording stops. No audio from the hold period is captured, including hold music or anything the caller hears.

docs.ex: Screen masks when voice masks. From ScreenAgent 2.1.40, masking a voice recording stops active screen recordings until unmask or the end. Playback shows a blank screen. Install steps stay on the Windows and Mac pages. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: When an agent masks a recording, the screen recording stops until the interaction is unmasked or ends.

docs.ex: Where a recording is found. Search and playback, the Contact History report, the Recording Activity report, and Cloud Storage Services are the places the page names. Column lists are not invented. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The page says you can search interactions to play back and download, delete recordings, see what is getting recorded with the Recording Activity report, and access record

docs.ti: QM is real, and this lab stays inside the page
docs.ex: QM is real, and this lab stays inside the page. Recording exists to support Quality Management. The supervisor certification names QM. This lesson does not invent evaluation forms, scores, or calibration rules. The recording overview says the product supports Quality Management processes and compliance. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The recording overview says the product supports Quality Management processes and compliance. That is the relationship this lab will defend.

docs.ti: Engagement Hub feeds QM from other systems
docs.ex: Engagement Hub feeds QM from other systems. Engagement Hub brings PABX, ACD, CRM, digital, and dialer data into CXone so Supervisor, Copilot for Supervisors, QM, and WFM can use it. Engagement Hub connects third-party systems such as PABXs, ACDs, CRMs, digital channels, and dialers to CXone. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Engagement Hub connects third-party systems such as PABXs, ACDs, CRMs, digital channels, and dialers to CXone.

docs.ex: Playback rules you can defend. A hold gap, a mask blank, and a third-party path are three different playback stories. Cloud storage is named. Retention numbers from other pages are not borrowed. Silence during hold is expected. A blank screen during a mask is expected from ScreenAgent 2.1.40. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Silence during hold is expected. A blank screen during a mask is expected from ScreenAgent 2.1.40.

docs.ex: Enlighten, Autopilot, and summaries. Autopilot (Omilia), voice versus chat, AutoSummary types, and Copilot on a foreign ACD. These are themed worlds inside Contact Path.
docs.eg: Autopilot (Omilia), voice versus chat, AutoSummary types, and Copilot on a foreign ACD.

docs.ex: Autopilot is Autopilot (Omilia). Autopilot (Omilia) is a virtual agent for voice and digital. It uses Experience Optimization data plus your interaction data. The Classics, Inc. story on the page is NiCE's example. NiCE CXone Autopilot (Omilia) handles voice and digital interactions in place of live agents. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: NiCE CXone Autopilot (Omilia) handles voice and digital interactions in place of live agents.

docs.ti: Voice and text do not connect the same way
docs.ex: Voice and text do not connect the same way. Voice uses a SIP backchannel and stays connected until complete or transfer. Text uses Virtual Agent Hub and the script on each turn. Voice setup needs NiCE. Text needs Digital Experience. A voice contact calls a number and may hit an IVR first. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: A voice contact calls a number and may hit an IVR first. Utterances are transcribed.

docs.ti: The four pieces of an Autopilot integration
docs.ex: The four pieces of an Autopilot integration. You need a configured channel, Virtual Agent Hub, a Studio script with a virtual agent action on the point of contact, and a configured Autopilot virtual agent. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The page requires NiCE CXone with a voice or digital chat channel, Virtual Agent Hub for provider connection and transcription options, at least one Studio script whose v

docs.ti: TTS voices and a knowledge base
docs.ex: TTS voices and a knowledge base. Standard TTS voices are in the subscription. Premium voices are bring-your-own. A knowledge base needs Knowledge Hub. This lesson does not invent prices. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Standard voices for Autopilot (Omilia) on the page include Omilia native, Google Standard, WaveNet, and Neural2, Microsoft Neural, and AWS Standard and Neural.

docs.ex: Three AutoSummary types. AutoSummary writes a summary after voice or digital messaging. Types are Structured AI, Generative AI, and Hybrid. Email is not supported. Agents can edit. Structured AI uses short phrases for intent, outcomes, and events. Generative AI is prose from the LLM. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Structured AI uses short phrases for intent, outcomes, and events. Generative AI is prose from the LLM.

docs.ex: What setup actually requires. An account representative enables AutoSummary and Agent Assist Hub. You then need a profile, Studio, skills with disposition, and a transcription profile. MAX also needs a Copilot for Agents license. You work with the account representative for the initial enablement. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: You work with the account representative for the initial enablement. Agent Assist Hub must be enabled.

docs.ti: Where the summary goes after the agent
docs.ex: Where the summary goes after the agent. Other agents see the summary only if it is mapped to a CRM. The Contact mapping uses Disposition Notes. A Final Summary API can return the AI text or the edited text for two days. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Without a CRM integration, other agents do not see the generated summaries. Mapping is on the Agent Integrations page: Contact entity type, NiCE CXone data field Disposit

docs.ex: CXone APIs. Register, pick a grant, discover the tenant, and keep access keys smaller than the person who minted them. These are themed worlds inside Contact Path.
docs.eg: Register, pick a grant, discover the tenant, and keep access keys smaller than the person who minted them.

docs.ex: Getting Started is a sequence. The developer Getting Started path is plan, register, a test user, authentication, discovery, and best practices. Registration is typically a few business days. This lesson does not invent a portal SLA. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Getting Started walks you through planning the integration, registering the application, creating a test user, choosing authentication, discovering your tenant's endpoint

docs.ti: Back-end apps use the password grant
docs.ex: Back-end apps use the password grant. A back-end integration uses OAuth 2.0 resource-owner password credentials. client_secret_basic puts the client in the Authorization header. client_secret_post puts it in the body. The API user has no login authenticator. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Back-end integrations on the authentication page use the OAuth 2.0 password grant. RFC 6749 defines that grant.

docs.ex: User-facing apps use OpenID Connect. A user login uses the authorization code flow. scope is openid. response_type is code. Confidential clients then exchange the code. PKCE S256 is the proof for public clients. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: User-facing applications follow OpenID Connect. The authentication page says the only supported scope value for CXone API authentication is openid, and the only supported

docs.ti: Discover the issuer, then the tenant
docs.ex: Discover the issuer, then the tenant. Start at the global issuer or the FedRAMP issuer, append OpenID configuration, and read token_endpoint. The tenant id from the ID token selects the CXone configuration. Do not hard-code na1. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The global issuer on the authentication page is https://cxone.niceincontact.com. Append /.well-known/openid-configuration.

docs.ti: Refresh early and pin the key id
docs.ex: Refresh early and pin the key id. Plan to renew before 5 minutes of access-token expiry. expires_in of 3600 is a sample. Verify JWTs with JWKS, cache keys 15 to 30 days, and reject an unknown kid. The token response includes expires_in. A sample on the page is 3600 seconds. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The token response includes expires_in. A sample on the page is 3600 seconds. The page also says each exchange can return a different lifetime, so you read the value you

docs.ti: An access key secret is shown once
docs.ex: An access key secret is shown once. If you miss the secret, mint another key. Disabling a key kills its tokens immediately. The key's power is the employee's power. The access-key pages and the connector guides say the same thing: copy the secret when you create it. If you lose it, create a new key. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The access-key pages and the connector guides say the same thing: copy the secret when you create it. If you lose it, create a new key.

docs.ti: Studio API actions are not the whole catalog
docs.ex: Studio API actions are not the whole catalog. Some APIs have Studio actions. Verb colors are documented. If no action exists, the traditional path is Snippet or a REST call. GET NEXT EVENT is for agent-application events. Not every API has an action. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The API actions page colors verbs: POST green, PUT orange, GET blue, DEL red, PATCH aqua. A purple shield marks security.

docs.ex: CRM integrations. Salesforce Lightning console, who gets billed, ticketing for Salesforce and Zendesk, and the IndexedDB reset. These are themed worlds inside Contact Path.
docs.eg: Salesforce Lightning console, who gets billed, ticketing for Salesforce and Zendesk, and the IndexedDB reset.

docs.ti: Salesforce wants Lightning and the console
docs.ex: Salesforce wants Lightning and the console. Agent Workspace for Salesforce is Lightning only. Console navigation keeps records on one screen. Standard navigation opens a new browser tab per interaction. The Salesforce Agent Workspace page says the integration is only available in Salesforce Lightning. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The Salesforce Agent Workspace page says the integration is only available in Salesforce Lightning. The org should use console navigation, not standard navigation.

docs.ti: Agent Integrations is a per-employee switch
docs.ex: Agent Integrations is a per-employee switch. Enable Customer Card and Agent Integrations on the employee. Billing follows the count of employees with Agent Integrations. The account representative enables Agent Integrations for the system. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: In Admin > Employees, enable Customer Card so agents can see the card. Enable Agent Integrations so they can use Agent Workspace for Salesforce and see Salesforce records

docs.ti: The script still has to change
docs.ex: The script still has to change. You need Scripts Create/Edit. The process is a CRM configuration, a Studio change, workflows, then optional manual create and optional reskill. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The page's process is: set up a CRM configuration for Salesforce, modify the Studio script, configure Salesforce workflows or configure them with ENHANCED WORKFLOW EXECUT

docs.ti: Einstein is a virtual agent, not the CRM screen
docs.ex: Einstein is a virtual agent, not the CRM screen. Salesforce Einstein connects through Virtual Agent Hub and TextBot Exchange for digital chat. It is not the same project as Agent Workspace inside Lightning. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The Einstein page connects Salesforce Einstein as a virtual agent through Virtual Agent Hub and TextBot Exchange. The channel is digital chat.

docs.ti: Ticketing currently names Salesforce and Zendesk
docs.ex: Ticketing currently names Salesforce and Zendesk. CRM Ticketing needs a license and Ticket Search permission. The FAQ says Salesforce and Zendesk are the supported CRMs. Users and name changes belong in the CRM. Tickets import when solved, and 90 days is the retention. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: You need a CRM Ticketing license and the Search & Playback > Search > Ticket Search permission. Tickets are searched in the Interactions application.

docs.ti: The channel list, including a repeated Slack
docs.ex: The channel list, including a repeated Slack. The ticketing page lists email, chat, Facebook, forum, in-app messaging, Slack, SMS, voice, WhatsApp, Telegram, Viber, Apple Messages for Business, Slack again, and Microsoft Teams. Slack appears twice. QM can evaluate a ticket. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The page's channel answer includes Email, Chat, Facebook, Forum, In App Messaging (SMS), Slack, SMS Messaging, Voice Calls, WhatsApp, Telegram, Viber, Apple Messages for

docs.ti: Salesforce Voice 26.3 needs one IndexedDB delete
docs.ex: Salesforce Voice 26.3 needs one IndexedDB delete. Upgrading the Salesforce Voice package from 26.2.8 or earlier to 26.3 requires deleting the IndexedDB database nice-cxone-ccf once. Package dates are not the whole platform's dates. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The IndexedDB page says that upgrading the Salesforce Voice package from 26.2.8 or earlier to 26.3 requires deleting the IndexedDB database named nice-cxone-ccf once.

docs.ex: Telephony and carriers. A leg and B leg, PSTN versus VoIP, softphones, allowlists, and TLS without invented SIP headers. These are themed worlds inside Contact Path.
docs.eg: A leg and B leg, PSTN versus VoIP, softphones, allowlists, and TLS without invented SIP headers.

docs.ti: A leg and B leg meet on a media server
docs.ex: A leg and B leg meet on a media server. The contact-to-CXone side is the A leg. The CXone-to-agent side is the B leg. Inbound treats A as ingress and B as egress. A transfer adds a second B leg. The contact calls a local or toll-free number. The call crosses the PSTN and enters CXone. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The contact calls a local or toll-free number. The call crosses the PSTN and enters CXone. That portion is the A leg, inbound or ingress.

docs.ti: PSTN is DID or TFN. VoIP stays on the agent leg.
docs.ex: PSTN is DID or TFN. VoIP stays on the agent leg.. CXone classifies DID or toll-free traffic as PSTN. It supports PSTN on the A leg and restricts VoIP to the agent leg, unless a UCaaS partner arrangement says otherwise. PSTN is the traditional phone system. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: PSTN is the traditional phone system. CXone classifies phone traffic routed by DID or toll-free number as PSTN.

docs.ti: Integrated Softphone is not the word WebRTC
docs.ex: Integrated Softphone is not the word WebRTC. Integrated Softphone is built in, with nothing to install. Softphone is a separate install. WebRTC is the Chrome technology Integrated Softphone uses. The names are not synonyms. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: If the agent leg is VoIP, CXone offers Integrated Softphone, built into the platform so there is nothing to install, and Softphone, a separate application that must be in

docs.ti: Numbers, RespOrg, and the voice PoP
docs.ex: Numbers, RespOrg, and the voice PoP. The preferred toll-free path is to make CXone the RespOrg. Local numbers can be ported. Other arrivals are remote call forwarding, an independent carrier, or your PBX. A voice PoP is the carrier's PSTN gateway. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The preferred option is to authorize CXone as the Responsible Organization for the toll-free numbers you want to use. Local numbers can be ported if you want that.

docs.ex: Allowlists, proxies, and TLS 1.2. Firewalls need the current domains, addresses, and ports. CXone does not support traffic-inspection proxies. Connections require at least TLS 1.2 and one of the ciphers the page lists for that direction. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The firewall section says domains, IP addresses, and ports must be allowed. The approved set is an allowlist. Copy it from the current help, not from this lesson.

docs.ti: Your tenant sits on a named cluster
docs.ex: Your tenant sits on a named cluster. CXone runs in AWS data centers that NiCE does not own. NiCE manages the software. A cluster has a letter-and-number name. You need your cluster when you work on connectivity. Users reach CXone with a browser and an internet connection. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Users reach CXone with a browser and an internet connection. There is no on-site computer running the CXone platform itself.

docs.ti: The carrier, the PoP, and CXone are three owners
docs.ex: The carrier, the PoP, and CXone are three owners. The carrier brings the internet and the voice PoP. CXone starts when the number, email, or chat is a point of contact. SIP header recipes and OPTIONS timers are not in the connectivity page. The carrier is the company that provides the internet connection. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The carrier is the company that provides the internet connection. The voice PoP is that carrier's PSTN gateway. A SIP trunk connects your PBX to the carrier.

docs.ex: UCCE, Avaya, and moved history. WFM connectors are not an ACD cutover. Multi-ACD versions, legacy Avaya, and Migrated Calls stay on their own pages. These are themed worlds inside Contact Path.
docs.eg: WFM connectors are not an ACD cutover. Multi-ACD versions, legacy Avaya, and Migrated Calls stay on their own pages.

docs.ti: Two migrations get confused on purpose
docs.ex: Two migrations get confused on purpose. A WFM connector copies agent state and history. Multi-ACD records a phone system you keep. Migrated Calls uploads old recordings. None of those pages is a full ACD cutover cookbook. The Cisco UCCE connector and the Avaya CMS pages feed Workforce Management. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The Cisco UCCE connector and the Avaya CMS pages feed Workforce Management. Engagement Hub and the Multi-ACD table record or process a third-party phone system.

docs.ti: The UCCE connector is on premises and speaks SQL
docs.ex: The UCCE connector is on premises and speaks SQL. The connector page supports Cisco Unified CCE 11.6. Real-time adherence uses the Cisco connector. Historical skills use SQL every 15 minutes. Intraday is not supported. Outbound dialer, fax, SMS, and web are no. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The connector is on-premise software. It receives agent state from the Cisco ACD and relays it for real-time adherence.

docs.ex: Web Setup must say AW-HDS-DDS. After install, verify PG data and the Administration and Data Server role. The role is Administration Server, Real-time and Historical Data Server, and Detail Data Server. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The page says to verify the Administration and Data Server role is AW-HDS-DDS: Administration Server, Real-time and Historical Data Server, and Detail Data Server.

docs.ti: Multi-ACD has its own Cisco and Avaya table
docs.ex: Multi-ACD has its own Cisco and Avaya table. UCCX 12.5 and 15 with NBR or BiB. UCCE 12.6 and 15. CUCM 12.5, 14, and 15, with a note that Cisco support for 12.5 ended 31 August 2025. Teams uses a recording bot and Graph library v1.2.0. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: On the Multi-ACD page, UCCX 12.5 and 15 use the UCCX CTI server and NBR or BiB. UCCE 12.6 and 15 use the UCCE CTI server. The dialer column names each product's dialer.

docs.ti: Avaya CMS and Avaya CMS Legacy are different connectors
docs.ex: Avaya CMS and Avaya CMS Legacy are different connectors. The current Avaya CMS page is an SDK over REST, inbound voice only, with intraday. The legacy ASC is version 19, on premises, SQL on Informix, and intraday is not supported. The Avaya CMS page connects through the SDK. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The Avaya CMS page connects through the SDK. Real-time and historical methods are REST APIs, at 15 minutes. Intraday is used in Intraday Manager.

docs.ti: Migrated Calls is a license, a format, and a list of vendors
docs.ex: Migrated Calls is a license, a format, and a list of vendors. You need the Migrated Interactions Upload license and the upload permission. Sources include Engage, CXone, Uptivity, and named third parties. Engage NMF plays back as MP4. Screen and digital do not migrate. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Migrated Calls needs the Migrated Interactions Upload license and Admin > Recording > Upload Migrated Interactions.

docs.ti: What a bridge design is allowed to say
docs.ex: What a bridge design is allowed to say. You can say how data is recorded or fed to WFM. You cannot say the ACD moved unless a page you cite says that. Account representatives and Professional Services own the gaps. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: A defensible bridge says which connector, which version page, which key employee, and which recording row.

docs.ex: Ecosystem, certifications, and the calendar. Credly badges without invented exam codes, the release cadence, and how to read a date that disagrees with the next page. These are themed worlds inside Contact Path.
docs.eg: Credly badges without invented exam codes, the release cadence, and how to read a date that disagrees with the next page.

docs.ti: Only the badges this lab opened
docs.ex: Only the badges this lab opened. Credly lists NCIE CXone ACD/IVR, NCIE CXone Mpower Digital Experience, NCAP CXone Mpower Workforce Management, NCAP CXone Mpower Personal Connection, and CXone Supervisor Certification. Exam codes are not on those badges. The ACD/IVR badge is NCIE CXone ACD/IVR. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The ACD/IVR badge is NCIE CXone ACD/IVR. Its badge text also uses the CXone Mpower ACD/IVR wording. Digital Experience has its own NCIE badge.

docs.ti: The supervisor badge comes through Club One
docs.ex: The supervisor badge comes through Club One. CXone Supervisor Certification is free and foundational. Its scope names WFM, QM, Dashboard, Coaching, and Gamification. Club One is the supervisor community that hosts it, not a catalog of every technical exam. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The Credly badge for CXone Supervisor Certification describes a free foundational certification reached through Club One.

docs.ti: How a release reaches a cluster
docs.ex: How a release reaches a cluster. Coming Soon starts about 30 days before beta. Final notes land on or just before beta. Customer clusters start about two weeks after beta, in groups. Control updates are about every three weeks. A major release is about four times a year. Dates are not guaranteed. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The release-process page describes Coming Soon about 30 days before beta, final notes on or just before beta, and customer clusters starting about two weeks after beta, i

docs.ti: 26.2 is a cycle with a rename table
docs.ex: 26.2 is a cycle with a rename table. The 26.2 cycle begins 29 April 2026 and the next cycle was targeted for 28 July 2026. Features can change. A rename example is CXone Mpower for Service Cloud Voice to Unified App for Salesforce Voice. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The 26.2 release notes say the cycle begins 29 April 2026 and that the next cycle was then targeted for 28 July 2026.

docs.ti: 26.3 and 26.4 disagree if you force one calendar
docs.ex: 26.3 and 26.4 disagree if you force one calendar. 26.3 moved to 2 September 2026 through 5 November 2026. Coming Soon for 26.4 begins 26 October 2026 and targets 4 February 2027. Those windows overlap. Controlled Release becomes Public Preview in 26.3. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The 26.3 notes say the cycle was originally 3 August 2026 to 25 October 2026 and, after a moratorium, 2 September 2026 to 5 November 2026. Features can change.

docs.ti: The cross-platform map is a set of pages
docs.ex: The cross-platform map is a set of pages. CUCM, UCCX, UCCE, and Teams each have a row on the Multi-ACD table. Webex versions are not invented. The ecosystem picture in this campus is a study map, and every edge needs a citation. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: UCCX 12.5 and 15, UCCE 12.6 and 15, and CUCM 12.5, 14, and 15 are Multi-ACD recording rows, with the 12.5 support note. The WFM connector's UCCE version is 11.6.

docs.ti: How to keep reading after this campus
docs.ex: How to keep reading after this campus. Re-open the page, prefer the sentence that names a version or a field, and mark a conflict instead of smoothing it. This campus is independent study. It is not NiCE, and the Studio export is not an official script. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: When two official sentences disagree, this campus quotes both. Priority pages, OIDC samples, release windows, and connector versions are the practice cases.

docs.ex: Skills routing and ACD. Dynamic delivery, routing attributes, channel lock, and what safe mode still routes. These are themed worlds inside Contact Path.
docs.eg: Dynamic delivery, routing attributes, channel lock, and what safe mode still routes.

docs.ti: Two ways dynamic delivery hands work out
docs.ex: Two ways dynamic delivery hands work out. Dynamic delivery routes on how long an agent has been Available and on proficiency. Automatic delivery paces about every 15 seconds. Agent-request delivery waits for Request Interaction or +1 Contact. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The dynamic delivery page says interactions route based on how long agents have been Available and on their proficiency in the skill.

docs.ti: Turn dynamic delivery on, and do not casually turn it off
docs.ex: Turn dynamic delivery on, and do not casually turn it off. The business unit's Contact Handling Method becomes Dynamic Delivery (Recommended). After that, NiCE recommends asking the account representative before you go back to static delivery. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The enable page's required permission is ACD > ACD Configuration > Business Unit Time Zones.

docs.ti: Routing attributes, five at a time
docs.ex: Routing attributes, five at a time. Attributes are custom traits inside a skill. Dynamic delivery can use several in one action. Static delivery can use one. More than five on one action can leave the contact with nobody. The routing attributes page calls them a bullseye method. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The routing attributes page calls them a bullseye method. They are custom traits that narrow the pool inside an ACD skill.

docs.ti: Proficiency for one user, or for one skill
docs.ex: Proficiency for one user, or for one skill. On dynamic delivery, the ACD user Skills tab changes many skills for one person. Changing many people on one skill is a different screen. The proficiency page is specific to dynamic delivery. Static delivery has its own help. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The proficiency page is specific to dynamic delivery. Static delivery has its own help. The required permission is ACD > Contact Settings > ACD Users Edit.

docs.ti: Channel lock, elevation, and integrated matching
docs.ex: Channel lock, elevation, and integrated matching. Channel lock turns AND into OR. Elevation has a table. Integrated matching compares voice, work items, and digital by priority, and it is on by default for new systems. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: With channel lock off, an agent whose Total Contact Count is 3 can have one voice interaction and two chats at the same time.

docs.ti: Least occupied, most occupied, and safe mode
docs.ex: Least occupied, most occupied, and safe mode. Tenant Management names Least Occupied and Most Occupied under advanced routing. Safe mode still routes, but routing attributes and bullseye ranges do not apply. Safe mode is a North America behavior. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The Manage Tenants page, under ACD advanced routing, describes Multiple Attributes as routing on more than one routing attribute.

docs.ex: Workforce management on the day. Real-time adherence every few seconds, intraday every 15 minutes, and the published schedule. These are themed worlds inside Contact Path.
docs.eg: Real-time adherence every few seconds, intraday every 15 minutes, and the published schedule.

docs.ti: Two clocks after the schedule exists
docs.ex: Two clocks after the schedule exists. Real-time adherence updates every few seconds. Intraday updates every 15 minutes and can reforecast the rest of the day. Historical adherence is a report. The Monitor page says that after the forecast and the schedules exist, you monitor both. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The Monitor page says that after the forecast and the schedules exist, you monitor both. Real Time Adherence compares scheduled WFM activities with events from the ACD.

docs.ti: The live table is only the current state
docs.ex: The live table is only the current state. RTA shows the current scheduled activity beside the current actual activity. A break that already ended is not on that table. Schedule edits show up almost immediately. The Real Time Adherence page requires WFM > General Permissions > Real Time Adherence set to ON. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The Real Time Adherence page requires WFM > General Permissions > Real Time Adherence set to ON. The table is a side-by-side of scheduled and actual activities.

docs.ex: Activity adherence or category adherence. A tenant uses one approach. If the category columns are on the table, adherence compares categories. Otherwise it compares activities. The page prints both examples. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The Real Time Adherence page says adherence is either activity-based or category-based, and only one is active.

docs.ti: Out of adherence, open, and severe
docs.ex: Out of adherence, open, and severe. Severe out of adherence is the headset icon: scheduled open, actual not open. Open versus a different open activity is out of adherence and OOA Open, but not severe. In adherence means the agent is doing the scheduled activity. Out of adherence means they are not. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: In adherence means the agent is doing the scheduled activity. Out of adherence means they are not.

docs.ti: Green dots, yellow dots, and 36 months
docs.ex: Green dots, yellow dots, and 36 months. A generated schedule remembers which forecast or staffing file it used. Green means published for all skills. Yellow means specific skills. Schedule Manager purges data older than 36 months. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Schedule Manager reviews and edits the schedule WFM generated from the staffing plan you created or uploaded in forecasting.

docs.ti: Fix the live row from Schedule Manager
docs.ex: Fix the live row from Schedule Manager. If the agent should be on break, change the activity in Schedule Manager and publish. RTA updates almost immediately. The CSV export covers up to 30 days and leaves unmapped activities uncalculated. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The Real Time Adherence page says you can put the agent back in adherence by editing the current activity in Schedule Manager and publishing.

docs.ex: Quality and Interaction Analytics. Evaluation forms, two average-score formulas, categories, and sentiment windows. These are themed worlds inside Contact Path.
docs.eg: Evaluation forms, two average-score formulas, categories, and sentiment windows.

docs.ti: Forms, plans, and no retention rule
docs.ex: Forms, plans, and no retention rule. Quality Management builds forms and plans, then can lead to coaching. The welcome page says there is no defined rule for how long evaluations must be kept. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The Quality Management welcome page says you build evaluation forms and plans, distribute interactions for evaluation, and may then design coaching.

docs.ex: 70 percent is not 73.3333. The welcome page walks Sanity QA through both formulas. Averaging the percentages gives 70. Averaging the points gives 73.3333. The page's Vijay figures do not match each other. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The welcome page's percentage table gives Sanity QA 3 ÷ 5 × 100 = 60% and 8 ÷ 10 × 100 = 80%.

docs.ti: A form is questions, then an activation
docs.ex: A form is questions, then an activation. Forms can be standard, self-assessments, or collaborative. A draft cannot be used. A critical answer can fail the whole evaluation. The supervisor review window on the form settings is 30 days. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: Form Manager says a form is a collection of questions used to evaluate interactions.

docs.ex: Categories, up to 2,000. Interaction Analytics categories are groups of transcript data. The system supports up to 2,000. Workspace edits wait until you click Update Data. A deleted category does not come back. The Categories page says categories are the foundation of Interaction Analytics. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The Categories page says categories are the foundation of Interaction Analytics. They are data groups used to parse transcripts.

docs.ti: Beginning, end, and three seconds of silence
docs.ex: Beginning, end, and three seconds of silence. Overall sentiment is the whole interaction. Beginning sentiment is the first 400 words or the first 30 percent, whichever comes first. End sentiment is the last 30 percent. Mixed is not available on the beginning or the end. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The Improve Sentiment page says you can filter a workspace by Positive, Negative, Neutral, or Mixed sentiment, and by when it occurred. Overall is the whole interaction.

docs.ti: JSON every 400 records, and closed tickets
docs.ex: JSON every 400 records, and closed tickets. Interaction Analytics can export JSON every 400 records or every 6 minutes, whichever comes first. The data page names four prebuilt reports. Closed or resolved CRM tickets can be searched for evaluation. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The data and reporting page says Interaction Analytics can export to a secure external bucket.

docs.ex: CRM, CTI, and CPaaS. Salesforce CTI URLs from the public pages, Integration Hub limits, and a CPaaS line with no URL. These are themed worlds inside Contact Path.
docs.eg: Salesforce CTI URLs from the public pages, Integration Hub limits, and a CPaaS line with no URL.

docs.ex: The Salesforce CTI adapter URL. Agent Workspace for Salesforce is Lightning only. The install creates two call centers. The non-FedRAMP CTI adapter URL and the FedRAMP URL are different hosts. Anything under 365 pixels wide is not supported. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The install page says Agent Workspace for Salesforce runs in Salesforce Lightning and is compatible with Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, and Marketing Cloud.

docs.ex: Trusted URLs and Click2Jack. Salesforce must trust cxagent.nicecxone.com and api.incontact.com. Click2Jack wants your own Lightning and My Domain hosts. It can block non-agent users who still carry NiCE components. The install page says to add cxagent.nicecxone.com and api.incontact.com as trusted URLs. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The install page says to add cxagent.nicecxone.com and api.incontact.com as trusted URLs.

docs.ti: A second CTI URL, 340 pixels wide
docs.ex: A second CTI URL, 340 pixels wide. Fully integrated Lightning uses /apex/icAgentConsole__agent, height 700, and width 340. That is not the embedded adapter URL and not the 420-pixel width. The fully integrated Lightning page says that after users are on the call center profile, you edit that call center. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
docs.eg: The fully integrated Lightning page says that after users are on the call center profile, you edit that call center.

docs.ex: Integration Hub: 50 connections, 32 KB. Integration Hub stores REST connections so Studio does not hold tokens in plain text. My Connections holds at most 50 connections. Each connection holds at most 50 requests. Responses are limited to 32 KB. Unconfirmed on this page. Source checked 2026-10 (month).
